newsitem.title: USA: Harley-Davidson posts record profits; recalls some bikes.
newsitem.headline: Harley-Davidson posts record profits; recalls some bikes.

text.p: Harley-Davidson Inc. Wednesday reported record profits for the third quarter on strong sales of motorcycles and an improved parts and accessories business.
The company also announced that it is voluntarily recalling 176,915 motorcycles manufactured during the 1994 to 1997 model years and sold in the United States and Canada.
"The vehicles use a vacuum-operated valve which could affect the supply of fuel to the carburettor," Harley said.
The Milwaukee-based company said it earned $33.2 million, or 44 cents a share, in the latest quarter, up from earnings of $23.7 million, or 32 cents a share, a year ago.
Sales increased 18 percent to $385.8 million from $327.1 million, it said.
Following the earnings news, Harley-Davidson's stock jumped $2.375 to $46.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said it shipped 28,013 motorcycles in the third quarter, up 3,001 units from a year ago. Parts and accessories sales totalled $90.5 million, up from $75.8 million last year.
"We're on track with our production capacity expansion efforts and are scheduled to ship 118,000 units in 1996," said Richard Teerlink, chairman and chief executive officer.
Last year, the company shipped 105,100 units.
"Our new model year change-over was the smoothest in recent memory and our production facilities averaged 490 units per day, with very minimal assembly line overtime," Teerlink said.
